# disc-probe

[English](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | Simplified Chinese

Let an ordinary optical drive measure a disc's spiral geometry by itself, then burn images onto the data side of a DVD-R or CD-R. The whole process requires no photographing or point-marking.

*Along the River During the Qingming Festival* (《清明上河图》), burned onto a Ritek F1 DVD-R, is the direct output: all of the geometry comes from read timing. This disc was burned only once, with no test burns, photo-based calibration, or scan correction. The photo was taken with a phone, cropped to the disc surface only, downscaled, and the background blurred.

## How it works

Burning an image onto the data side requires knowing which angle on the disc the Nth sector lands at. Each batch of discs has tiny differences in track pitch and bit length, and over tens of thousands of revolutions these accumulate and twist the image into a swirl. The common remedy is to burn a calibration pattern, mark points on a photo, and correct repeatedly.

disc-probe lets the drive do the measuring. When the disc spins at constant speed, the moment a sector finishes reading is the moment it rotates under the read head. By reading two sectors in turn and converting the difference in their completion times into an angle, you learn how far apart they are on the disc. A single measurement only yields the remainder within 360°, so measurements proceed level by level from near to far, with each level using the previous results to predict the full revolution count. 22 levels for DVD and 36 for CD cover the whole disc.

This measurement issues only read commands. After measuring, you can generate an ISO directly, or export a [DiscImageStudio](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio) preset.

## Results

### Geometric accuracy

This is a local section of the grid test disc, scanned at 600 dpi on a flatbed scanner, high-pass filtered, about 38 mm square. This disc was likewise burned only once, using only timing results (HL-DT-ST GH70N, Ritek F1 DVD-R). Across 8 scans, the angular peak-to-peak value within 25–54 mm was 0.11°, with an RMS of 0.03°. At a 50 mm radius, 0.03° corresponds to roughly 0.03 mm.

The green line in the figure is this disc. The measurement plan was [pre-registered before burning](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/blob/HEAD/docs/PREREG_remeasure.md).

### Detail

Macro photos of a tiled disc, also burned only once. The impossible triangle is 4.2 mm wide, the little figures are 6.8 mm tall, and the topmost element is a triple-line group used to measure line width. The smallest 1 mm triangle is visible to the naked eye, and each of its edges is about 0.15 mm wide. A 600 dpi scan can separate 0.12 mm lines, 0.08 mm is marginal, and anything finer is at the limit of the scanner.

It can go finer still: the outer ring of the Qingming disc is drawn with a grid of about 4–6 µm. We have no microscope; these photos were taken with a phone and a reversed DSLR lens, each about 24 mm wide at roughly 10 µm per pixel, so individual grid cells are still below the scale a phone can resolve. The color is just diffraction from the disc itself. More photos are at…

# Sparkle 3

## Database and Automatic Migrations

The database is managed with Flyway. On application startup, it automatically checks for and runs migrations in `classpath:db/migration` that have not yet been applied. A brand-new database is built from `V1__initial_schema.sql`. A production database that already contains data has its current structure version identified in `FlywayMigrationConfig` and is baselined, so old table-creation or large-table migrations are not re-executed.

The production environment requires PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, the `pg_trgm` extension, and a database account with permission to create schema objects, indexes, and TimescaleDB policies. The `timescaledb` extension must be pre-installed by the database administrator. The application migrations only run `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS`.

Upgrade steps:

1. Back up the database and confirm that the `timescaledb` extension is available.
2. Deploy the new version once. Under the protection of a PostgreSQL advisory lock, Flyway automatically creates or updates `flyway_schema_history`. No manual SQL is needed.
3. Check the startup logs. When an existing database is adopted, the log records `Adopting existing Sparkle3 schema into Flyway at legacy version ...`. Subsequent incremental migrations are recorded normally by Flyway.
4. Future schema changes only require adding a `V<version>__<description>.sql` file. Changing the checksum of a published migration file is prohibited.

If an existing database has not yet completed the TimescaleDB conversion (`ban_history` is not a hypertable), the application refuses to adopt it automatically and displays a prompt. In that case, first use the historical scripts kept in `db_sql/` to complete one upgrade from `v20_convert_to_timescaledb.sql` through `v22_fuck_index.sql`, then start the new version.

## Frontend Development

The frontend uses Vue 3, TypeScript, Vue Router, Pinia, and Arco Design Vue. Dependencies are managed uniformly with pnpm:

```bash
cd frontend
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

The dev server listens on `http://localhost:5173` by default and proxies `/api`, OAuth, and avatar requests to `http://localhost:7799`. The frontend supports Simplified Chinese and English, which can be switched live in the navigation bar. The language selection is saved in the browser's local storage.

Production builds are invoked automatically by Gradle, which calls pnpm and packages the Vite output into the Spring Boot jar:

```bash
pnpm --dir frontend build…
```

# Coding2API

Ten channels, namely **CodeBuddy** (mainland China and international, as two separate channels), **TRAE SOLO**, **OpenCode Zen**, **Kilo**, **Qoder**, **CodeArts**, **OfficeAce**, **小浣熊**, and **灵犀**, are wrapped into an OpenAI-compatible API with a shared credential pool, unified model names and scheduling, and per-user usage statistics.

> [!WARNING]
> Reverse-engineered interfaces, for study and research only, with no security audit performed. Public deployment requires a reverse proxy, authentication, and an IP allowlist.

## Features

- **OpenAI-compatible endpoints**: `/v1/chat/completions` (streaming / non-streaming), `/v1/responses` (Codex CLI), `/v1/messages` (Claude Code), `/v1/models` (including single-model lookup), `/v1/user/balance`.
- **Unified scheduling**: flat names pick credentials by health; `model@channel` forces a specific channel. Priority: free channels, then fewest in-flight requests, then quota expiring soonest, then health plus tiered cooldown, then highest balance. Admins can set a **weight** on a credential (`-1000..1000`). It only reorders within the same health tier (positive values preferred, negative values as backup) and never pushes cooled-down or exhausted credentials to the front. The x0 multiplier in the catalog is calibrated against actual charges measured over the last 24h, so that if upstream changes its billing without updating the catalog, a model does not stay stuck in the free tier forever. Model-level rate limits only avoid that model. Multi-turn conversations stick to the same credential and rotate only on error.
- **Expiring quota first**: the primary window (default 36h) consumes quota that is about to expire first; ties are broken by the 7-day window. Units are unified as credits.
- **Model lists loaded per credential**: only channels with usable credentials are listed, so there are no ghost models.
- **Shared credential pool**: maintained by admins, shared by all users, and encrypted at rest (`APP_SECRET`). Includes device-code login, multi-account switching, quota probing, check-in, and token pre-refresh.
- **Three roles**: `admin` / `operator` / `viewer`, stored in SQLite. Features one-time activation links, forced password change on first login, and immediate session revocation when a role is changed or an account is deactivated. Logins and write operations are audited.
- **Growth center** (CodeBuddy only): claim gifts, dispatch Buddy, claim task rewards, backfill missed logins, redeem streak rewards, and open blind boxes. Irreversible actions are disabled with `GROWTH_IRREVERSIBLE_ACTIONS=false`.
- **Redacted statistics**: conversations are not stored. Detail records are kept for 90 days and hourly summaries permanently. Visualized by user, channel, model, and credential. Costs are estimated from OpenRouter list prices. Speed is split into body and total output. Details are streamed over SSE.
- **Monthly billing** (`operator` and above): monthly summaries of requests, tokens, and costs by user or by API Key. Export as CSV (by user) or JSONL (per-record detail), with exports written to the audit log. Per-key detail is subject to the 90-day retention limit.

# dart-insight

dart-insight is a disclosure analysis web service that compares two DART periodic reports and shows the changed financial figures and sentences along with their original-text evidence. Even people unfamiliar with disclosures can search for a company without logging in, pick two periodic reports from the same company, and check what changed.

> The service name (Dart Insight or 공시레이더) has not been decided yet. Planning, scope, and decisions are based on Notion. See [Documentation guide](#문서-안내) below.

## MVP scope

**Flow:** Company search → report selection → comparison validation → analysis in progress → results (summary, changes in financial figures, changes in sentences) → check original text

| Category | Content |
| --- | --- |
| MVP (P1) | Company search, list of periodic reports and whether they are corrected, selection of comparison reports and validation of comparability, comparison of financial accounts, detection of changes in body text and tables and their prioritization, evidence-based summaries, evidence for figures and sentences and their location in the DART original, automatic check for investment-solicitation expressions |
| Extension priority 1 | Citation verification → audit log and Kill Switch → ML anomaly detection |
| Extension (P2) | Login, favorites, and new-disclosure alerts; review, approval, and publishing; AI recommendation of comparison criteria; section filters; sentence change history |
| Not included | Buy/sell recommendations, target prices, stock price forecasts |

The purpose and completion criteria for each issue are in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/ShinhanDSProject/dart-insight/issues). Issues are managed only on GitHub.

## Tech stack and folders

| Folder | Role | Technology |
| --- | --- | --- |

# 智膳 AI｜Multimodal Intelligent Cooking Conversational Agent

> An intelligent cooking assistant that combines multimodal large models, six-stage RAG retrieval, an explicit LangGraph Agent Workflow, deterministic Grounding for anti-hallucination, and tool-calling capabilities. 智膳 AI is a multimodal conversational Agent application for everyday cooking. Users can upload photos of ingredients, speak by voice, or type text requests. The system automatically recognizes intent and calls the matching tools (recipe knowledge base retrieval, nutrition calculation, shopping list generation, web search, recipe favoriting). It remembers users' long-term preferences such as dietary restrictions and allergies across multiple conversation turns, and returns results in a streaming fashion.

What sets this project apart from an ordinary demo is that it does not use `create_react_agent` as a one-line shortcut. Instead, it hand-builds a **three-path explicit workflow** on LangGraph `StateGraph`, with intent routing, toolsets, and System Prompts isolated per node. It also implements engineering designs such as **closure-level user identity binding**, **full-chain RAG degradation**, **two-layer anti-hallucination for tool parameters**, and **zero-extra-LLM-call deterministic output grounding (Grounding)**. Core pain points it addresses:

- Recipe recommendations and nutrition calculation are scattered across different apps, making the workflow fragmented
- LLMs that generate recipes directly carry hallucination risks, such as absurd ingredient quantities, unauthorized favoriting, and fabricated numbers
- Negations and dietary constraints (“no spicy”, “halal”) are naturally ineffective in vector space, so retrieval results are unreliable

chinjiaqing/jc-daily-report.body:
# ⚽ Football Signal Radar · Daily Signal Report

> **Set emotion aside, watch only the signals.**
> Cross-validation of line movements across three channels. No bets at low odds, no bets when signals are unclear. Pre-match execution is automatic, and post-match settlement is automatic.

## 🚀 Online Site

- **[https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/](https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/)**
- Updated automatically every hour, with historical dates archived for review at any time
- Covers 500–1,300+ matches per day (full Jingcai and Asian handicap coverage), with signals and bets automatically flagged

---

## Detours We Skipped

We tried **models**: we piled up parameters until the room was full. Looking back, a model only recited prices the market had already set. No matter how many parameters we added, it could not produce anything new.

We tried **studying the bookmakers' moves**: guessing at the house's tactics, and the more we guessed, the more it looked like paranoid delusion. Eventually we realized that guessing the bookmaker is less useful than watching the price.

We also tried **AI predictions**: injuries, motivation, form. Every point sounded convincing, and every one had already been priced into the odds. However lively the talk, the line doesn't care.

After the detours, one plain truth remains:

> **Where the money flows, the line speaks.**
> But people watching the line get carried away easily: chasing favorites, fearing upsets, shaky hands near kickoff. You can tell at a glance that emotion is doing the trading.

So we hand both "watching" and "buying" to the machine, and keep just one thing for humans: **discipline**.

## Three Informants, One Referee

**European odds (1X2)** track market-wide odds movements: who is collectively abandoning a side, who is quietly defending, and whether the draw line has been given up. This is the informant closest to the action.

**Asian handicap** tracks lines and water (odds): sudden pivots near kickoff, sharp money backing the top side. The money is real cash, which speaks more plainly than what people say.

**Over/Under** tracks the total goals line. Once a goal-scoring hotbed appears, the number of goals in the match is often already predictable.

Each informant has its own news. When the news matches, the referee dares to call it. **Matches where they disagree (European odds and Asian handicap fighting each other) are simply left alone**: if the informants are already arguing, there is no reason to bet.

## Discipline Matters More Than Vision

Once the direction is set, everything else is discipline:

- **No bets at low odds**: single-selection odds under 1.5, or double-selection odds that discount below 1.3. No matter how good the signal, it isn't bought. At odds that low, even a win doesn't make real money.
- **No bets without clear signals**: no signal, conflicting signals, or a vague direction means always wait. Missing out loses no money; betting wrong does.
- **Quality decides stake size**: the stronger the signal, the larger the stake (1, 2, or 4 units). No all-in gambling.
- **Bets are placed automatically 15 minutes before kickoff, and results are settled automatically when they come in**: no shaky hands in the moment, and no urge to raise stakes after winning or chase losses after losing.

---

## ⚠️ Disclaimer

This project is for data research only and does not constitute any betting advice. Buy lottery tickets only at licensed physical retail outlets. Anyone under 18 years old may not participate.

jiuchai/fish-house.body:
# Big Fish's Little House

> A video wallpaper plugin for AstrBot: each node on the theme canvas is a video clip, and the wallpaper plays out according to how the nodes are connected.

**v3.0.2** · AstrBot >= 4.9.0 · Vue 3 + Element Plus panel · MIT License

---

## Introduction

'Big Fish's Little House' turns a character into an animated video wallpaper:

- When idle, it plays an idle video on a looping node;
- When a message arrives, it follows the canvas connections to the 'Reply to Message' node, and the QQ reply is only sent once the character actually picks up the phone;
- When an action node finishes, it automatically continues along the outgoing edge; when there are multiple branches, the model chooses based on the node descriptions;
- Nodes are joined with cross-fades, so multiple videos never compete for frames;
- The bottom speech bubble is generated by the model on the fly and fades out after 3 seconds;
- It has a standalone wallpaper page that can be added directly as an OBS browser source or used as a desktop wallpaper.

The entire runtime does not rely on built-in fixed action slots; everything is driven by the current theme's canvas.

---

## Core Concepts

| Concept | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Theme | A complete configuration: cover, asset library, canvas, and settings, packaged as a single `.zip` |
| Project | The editing state of a theme. Each theme has one project; assets, cover, and canvas are saved independently |
| Asset library | The video pool within a project. Nodes select assets and do not bind file paths directly |
| Canvas node | A video clip plus a character type; nodes are connected into a runtime path |
| Bubble | A one-line message at the bottom of the wallpaper, generated by the model; 3 seconds by default |
| Wallpaper page | `/fish_house/index.html`; viewable without logging in to AstrBot |

---

## How the Canvas-Driven Flow Works

1. On receiving a private message, if the current node is a loop node with only one outgoing edge → automatically move to the next node;
2. If there are multiple outgoing edges → pass the current node, the available outgoing edges, and each node's description to the model, and require it to call `house_flow_goto` to choose one;
3. If the model only replies without switching nodes → after the reply is sent, fall back to the first outgoing edge to avoid getting stuck;
4. One-shot nodes (action/transition) play through for the asset's duration and then automatically take the first outgoing edge; a `phone` node also puts the phone down and continues after one round;
5. If the canvas contains a 'Reply Only' node, replies wait until the wallpaper reaches that node before being sent (waiting at most 10 seconds; if it times out, the reply is sent anyway).

There is no keyword matching and no fixed commands; which route is taken is decided by the model's tool calls.

### Node Types

| Type | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Loop wait | Stays in place waiting for a message; continues along the outgoing edge once one arrives |
| Reply/Work | Can reply to messages and accept tasks; continues after one minute of idle |
| Reply/Work (leave when done) | Same as above; continues immediately when the task ends |
| Work only | Only accepts tasks; continues after one minute of idle |
| Work only (leave when done) | Only accepts tasks; continues immediately when the task ends |
| Reply only | Only replies to messages; the QQ reply is actually sent only when this node is reached |
| Action | Plays once, then continues along the outgoing edge |

# Douyin Live Room Go-Live/Offline Monitor

Automatically monitors a list of Douyin live rooms. As soon as a room goes live or goes offline, a notification is pushed to iPhone via Bark. Tapping the notification uses the Douyin URL Scheme (`snssdk1128://live`) to open Douyin directly into the corresponding live room.

## How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[External scheduler / GitHub Actions trigger] --> B[Run monitor.py]
    B --> C[Read rooms.txt]
    C --> D[Request live.douyin.com/room one by one]
    D --> E{Page contains m3u8/flv stream address?}
    E -- Yes --> F[Mark as live]
    E -- No --> G[Mark as offline]
    F & G --> H[Compare with last state]
    H --> I[Send Bark if state changed]
    I --> J[Tap notification to open Douyin live room]
```

Detection basis: the `liveStatus` field in Douyin's web SSR data also returns `normal` for rooms that are live (unreliable). However, offline room pages contain zero real stream addresses such as `m3u8/flv/pull_url`, while live rooms contain many. Therefore, "the page contains real stream addresses" is used as the reliable signal for a room being live. If the page cannot be fetched or an error occurs, no notification is sent for that run (to prevent false alarms).

## File Overview

- `monitor.py` — main program: reads rooms.txt, detects go-live, sends Bark notifications, writes state.json.
- `rooms.txt` — monitoring list. Only this file needs to be edited; there is no need to touch monitor.py.
- `state.json` — runtime state (last live status), maintained automatically by the program and already added to .gitignore.
- `add_room.ps1` — script for adding rooms from the local command line, independent of this tool (see below).
- `add_room.py` — Python version of the same functionality (backup).
- `.github/workflows/douyin-monitor.yml` — GitHub Actions workflow (native schedule as a fallback).

## rooms.txt Format

One room per line, in the form "link or identifier, display name", separated by a comma:

    https://live.douyin.com/125093611494, Teacher Zicheng's Family Education Lessons
    https://v.douyin.com/1_AyxhJoFkc/, Yuchuan E-commerce

- The display name may be omitted (short links automatically look up the nickname using sec_uid).

# PerkRadar

PerkRadar is a self-deployable aggregator of deal leads. It periodically reads a fixed set of public RSS, Atom, JSON, and Markdown sources, organizes titles, original links, and short summaries into a lightweight SQLite database, and then uses a web dashboard to help you search, filter, bookmark, and mark items as claimed.

Entries come from public feeds and may include chit-chat, wanted posts, promotions, or expired offers. Categories are inferred from title rules and do not verify whether a deal is genuine, its validity period, or your eligibility to claim it. Please refer to the original post and the official terms of the offer.

## Deployment

We recommend having Personal Agent help with deployment, or you can run it yourself by following the steps below. PerkRadar is suited to single-host, single-instance deployment and requires a long-running Node process and a writable local SQLite data directory.

- **Local use**: binds to `127.0.0.1:38471` by default. If authentication is not enabled, use it only in a trusted single-user environment.
- **Public use**: access it through a TLS reverse proxy and set `PERKRADAR_ACCESS_TOKEN` to a random value of at least 32 characters. The application port should remain open only to the host.

External push notifications can be integrated separately by the caller. PerkRadar itself does not send notifications.

- **Docker method**: Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2.24 or later. Docker Desktop also works. Node.js does not need to be installed on the host.

### Get the Source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/luobinger/PerkRadar.git

```

This command builds the production image and starts the container. SQLite data is stored in `./data` on the host. The container runs as the non-root `node` user (uid 1000), so the host data directory must be writable by that user. wlrwx/football-engine.description: Sporttery football probability analysis system - Dixon-Coles + Monte Carlo integrated model, fully automated on GitHub Actions
wlrwx/football-engine.body:
# Sporttery Engine

A probability analysis and virtual betting simulation system for Sporttery football. It is based on the Dixon-Coles Poisson model and Monte Carlo simulation, uses market-dominated probability fusion, allocates virtual bets with the Kelly criterion, and runs fully automatically on GitHub Actions at zero server cost. **For data analysis and algorithm learning only. It does not constitute any betting advice; all outputs are virtual bookkeeping.**

## Core Principles (driven by 2026-08 empirical data)

1. **The market is the benchmark**: Across 426 matches in the ledger, the pure market (vig-removed) Brier score of 0.583 beats every model stream (0.646+). The fusion weight is therefore market-dominated (0.75), and models and third-party sources only make minor adjustments.
2. **Every switch is decided by data**: each step of the fusion chain is a config switch (`config/prediction.json["fusion"]["post_fusion"]`). `scripts/ablation_replay.py` decides whether each one stays or goes, by paired replay over settled ledgers.
3. **Self-evolution with guardrails**: any automatic enabling of the calibration layer or LGBM must pass a time-based split and a paired significance test. If performance degrades, it is automatically disabled. See `docs/UPGRADE2_20260829.md`.

## Architecture

```
Daily loop: fetch data → fusion prediction (fusion.py, fully traced) → lock → settle → self-learning
Weekly loop: backtest → weight optimization (champion/challenger) → parameter refit → Monday health check
Evolution loop: clean samples (chain=v2) accumulate → calibration layer auto-revives/disables (calibration_auto)
                      → LGBM shadow training + validation (lgbm_shadow) → weekly effect judgment (tracker)
```

## Tech Stack

- Python 3.12 / numpy / scikit-learn / LightGBM / joblib
- GitHub Actions (computation) + GitHub Pages (reports)
- No database; plain CSV/JSON with git versioning; the ledger is append-only

## Directory Structure

```
engine/
├── prediction/     # dixon_coles / monte_carlo / fusion (pure functions + switches + trace) / lgbm
├── strategy/       # kelly / odds-signal gate / hot-zone stake sizing / edge capping / three-ticket system
├── learning/       # fusion_optimizer (automatic weight tuning) / calibration_auto (calibration self-evolution)
│                   # lgbm_shadow (shadow training) / league_params / elo
├──…
```

# yan-skills

Agent Skills for people doing SEO and indie development. **Building sites, picking keywords, getting backlinks, checking data, and reviewing and iterating**. The whole pipeline lives in this repo, and it runs as soon as you install it.

By [Yan](https://github.com/yan-labs). Polished for personal use and tested in practice. Compatible with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, and any platform that reads `SKILL.md`. MIT license, so take it and use it freely.

```bash
npx skills add yan-labs/yan-skills -g --all
```

---

## What problem this solves

A person running a standalone site typically spends a day like this:

In the morning they want to start a new direction, so they first check whether the keyword has search volume and how hard it is to rank for. Tool websites charge two hundred dollars a month, which is too expensive, so they open a dozen tabs and compare by hand. At noon they settle on a keyword and start building the site: scaffolding, Cloudflare, domain, GA, GSC. The whole process takes two days, and next time they build a site they go through it again and hit the same pitfalls. In the afternoon they need backlinks, so they dig up a "500 free backlink sites" list someone shared and open the first twenty. Seventeen don't open, two require registration and review, and one asks you to link to him first. In the evening they open GSC, see "Crawled - currently not indexed," and don't know whether to change the content or submit again.

Three months later they switch to another project, and the whole set above starts from scratch again.

**This repo exists to end the "start from scratch again."** It turns each of the steps above into scripts, data files, and judgment rules that AI agents can follow directly.
